root_cause_criterion.criterion: At the Arabic in-place reorder call site, the cluster-merge helper must operate on the live `buffer->info` array rather than the stale pre-decomposition `buffer->out_info` array. On the crash path the vulnerable call still uses `merge_out_clusters(start, j)` after `swap_buffers()`, so the actual cluster source differs from the live array on the protected merge event.
root_cause_criterion.description: The selected root obligation is that the merge helper used by `reorder_marks_arabic()` must read cluster state from the current live `buffer->info` array. The vulnerable event violates that obligation by selecting stale `buffer->out_info`, while the fixed event satisfies it on the same protected merge.
root_cause_criterion.verification_note: The vulnerable assertion trace shows `actual_cluster_base != required_cluster_base` at `arabic_cluster_merge`, and the fixed assertion trace shows equality at the same `span_end=17` event.

nodes.state: At the crash-leading `merge_out_clusters()` dispatch loop, the current live range still has `end > out_len` (`17 > 16` in the frozen trace), so the helper is operating over a span that already extends beyond the stale pre-decomposition output length. By source semantics, that means the preceding cluster scan necessarily ranged into the stale old-`info` tail.

`set_cluster()` is reached with `&info` equal to the `&out_info[i]` slot dispatched by `merge_out_clusters()`, so the sink is operating on the stale output-buffer element selected by the wrong helper.

edges.relation: The same live mark-run end index `j` computed by `reorder_marks_arabic()` is passed unchanged as `end` into `merge_out_clusters()`, carrying the in-place live span into the stale-buffer helper.

The same `out_info[i]` slot pointer emitted at the vulnerable dispatch loop is the `info` reference observed at the subsequent `set_cluster()` sink, so the stale helper selection reaches the crashing sink unchanged.
